cells.tense: You are moving toward what you're for, at a pace you can keep.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Take the step that's actually next, using only what you can already reach. Leave everything past it dark for now. Move, and find out by going.
cells.core:
When something moves you, you move, and the moving keeps correcting itself — more of this, less of that — without a lurch. That's the part that works: feeling turns into direction, and the direction stays adjustable. The road doesn't need to be visible all the way; it needs the next stretch of it, and you take that.

The practice is to stop waiting for the whole map. Take the step that's actually next, using only what you can already reach. Leave everything past it dark for now. Wanting a complete plan before the first move is the part that isn't helping — one small correction on the way will teach you more than a month of figuring.
cells.sheetLine: Enough for the next step is enough.
cells.verb: to move toward what you're for
cells.place: on the move, keeping your footing while everything shifts

cells.tense: You will reach the next thing before you have finished arriving at this one.
cells.act: adjust one dial a little, then stop
cells.ask: Change one setting — how much, how fast, how close — a little toward easier. Then leave it alone for a day. Watch the smaller setting before you reach again.
cells.core:
The drive doesn't stop when the thing is done; it goes looking for somewhere else to put the weight, and finds somewhere before you've noticed. The next goal gets started while the last one is still arriving. Then the moving stops being steered and starts steering, and the destination rushes at you with your own momentum behind it.

Correct it small and immediately. Change one setting — how much, how fast, how close — a little toward easier, then leave it alone for a day. Watch the smaller setting before you reach again. The first day will feel like idling. It isn't; it's the correction taking hold. What's at the far end of the drive has to finish arriving, or by the time you get there you'll already be past it.
cells.sheetLine: The next thing starts before the last one lands.

cells.tense: You were moved toward something, and you have been standing still.
cells.act: let the thing end that is already over
cells.ask: Something you were carrying as open is already finished — done, gone, or long past deciding. Let it be finished. Not a plan for after. Stop counting it as live.
cells.core:
The feeling is still here and the movement isn't. Something you were for has turned into a place you keep standing without leaving, and the standing has replaced the going. From inside it's hard to tell, because the feeling is warm enough to pass for motion. The current that would carry you isn't broken; it's held back by what you haven't let finish.

Something you were carrying as open is already finished — done, gone, or long past deciding. Let it be finished. Not a plan for after. Stop counting it as live. Take it off the list of things still in play. What you were moving toward gets its room back the moment the finished thing stops being carried as though it were live.
cells.sheetLine: You feel the pull without moving, because something is still open.

cells.tense: You are steering something here without knowing you have your hand on it.
cells.act: stop holding up the false thing and watch it come down
cells.ask: Find where your effort is the only thing keeping something standing. Lift that effort off it for a week. Watch what happens. Don't put it back.
cells.core:
There's movement here you didn't start and can't feel, because it's woven in far enough that you'd call it the situation. Things keep heading somewhere you didn't choose, or nothing has moved in a long while and you'd say that's just how it is. From inside, either one reads as given. But the effort holding it in place is being made, and the effort is yours.

Find where your effort is the only thing keeping something standing. Lift that effort off it for a week and watch what happens. Don't put it back. If it stands without you, you've learned what's real. If it comes down, it was yours to set down. Either way the next move is yours, and you'll know it's yours because now you can see who was making it.
cells.sheetLine: The effort holding it up is yours, and you didn't know.

cells.place: on the move, keeping your footing while everything shifts
